scope: Research reconnaissance for an iid two-free-parameter zero-truncated NB existence/uniqueness theorem, 1955 onward; not a formal manuscript bibliography audit.
provider: web search and primary-source web/local full-text reading
stopping_rule: 20 search queries, followed by primary-source acquisition and reading of the relevant accessible results
queries: "truncated negative binomial" maximum likelihood concavity theorem
"truncated negative binomial" likelihood uniqueness Sampford theorem Brass 1958
Brass 1958 "Simplified methods" truncated negative binomial pdf

readings.work: Sampford (1955), The Truncated Negative Binomial Distribution, Biometrika 42, 58–69
readings.locator: printed pp. 65–66, section 8, especially the end of section 8 on p. 66
readings.inspection: Read the two-page primary scan visually, including equations (15)–(17), endpoint conditions, and conjecture paragraph.
readings.finding: Two endpoint conditions are sufficient for at least one positive-size solution. Necessity and uniqueness are explicitly left conjectural. The two limits are Poisson and logarithmic series, not just Poisson.

readings.work: Wyshak (1974), Algorithm AS 68: A Program for Estimating the Parameters of the Truncated Negative Binomial Distribution, JRSS C 23, 87–91
readings.locator: pp. 87–91, especially description pp. 87–88, failure indicators p. 89, and code pp. 90–91
readings.inspection: Full primary PDF text read via web extraction.
readings.finding: Gives score iteration, starting values, observed second derivatives, failure indicators, examples, and Fortran code. No proof of joint necessity or uniqueness. Its stated variance-larger-than-mean applicability is not a proved iff criterion for the positive sample.

readings.work: Simon (1961), Fitting Negative Binomial Distributions by the Method of Maximum Likelihood
readings.inspection: Primary PDF acquired to ignored scratch; full text inspected locally.
readings.locator: printed pp. 47–48, equations (11)–(18); pp. 50–51, equations (35)–(38), iteration discussion and conclusion
readings.finding: Eliminates a freely adjusted zero mass to obtain the same score equations as positive truncation. Supplies an iterative numerical scheme and examples, but no necessity or uniqueness proof. The zero-distortion parameter is broader than nonnegative zero inflation, so its elimination does not remove the ZINB feasibility check.

readings.work: Brass (1958), Simplified Methods of Fitting the Truncated Negative Binomial Distribution, Biometrika 45, 59–68
readings.inspection: Publisher metadata available; PDF redirects to purchase page through web, HTTP 403 on direct download.
readings.finding: Proof not inspected; unresolved coverage gap.

readings.work: Sanathanan (1977), Estimating the Size of a Truncated Sample
readings.inspection: Search preview only; publisher full-text request returned HTTP 403.
readings.finding: Asymptotic population-size theory is advertised; no finite-sample uniqueness theorem verified.

readings.work: On the robustness of truncated negative binomial regression model: application to field epidemiology (accepted 2025)
readings.inspection: Search extraction supplied model, robustness results, and algorithm discussion; direct open hit a CAPTCHA.
readings.finding: Inspected extraction concerns regression robustness and numerical Hessian corrections, not a proof of the iid finite-sample conjecture. Not a full-text proof reading.

readings.work: Jayakumar and Sankaran (2020), A Generalization of Inverse Marshall-Olkin Family of Distributions
readings.finding: Search false positive: claimed uniqueness concerns an inverse truncated-NB Weibull continuous model, not the count model here. Not used as evidence about the conjecture.

conclusion: No later settlement verified within this search. This is not proof that the conjecture remains open in all literature; inaccessible Brass and other uninspected sources remain explicit gaps.
